evidence_spans.text:
In ASD, deleterious patterns of noise are consistently exacerbated 
with the presence of secondary (comorbid) neuropsychiatric diagnoses, lower verbal and performance 
intelligence, and autism severity.
evidence_spans.claim: Noise patterns in ASD worsen with comorbid diagnoses, lower IQ, and greater autism severity.

evidence_spans.text:
Importantly, such patterns in ASD are present whether or not the 
participant takes psychotropic medication.
evidence_spans.claim: The ASD motor-noise signature is independent of psychotropic medication status.

assessments.support: Explicit site-level inclusion rules (raw uncorrected scans, >=8 min scan duration, >=15 ASD individuals), yielding 7 of 16 ABIDE sites and 605 participants (304 ASD, 301 CT).
Per-site N by diagnosis reported (e.g. UM_1: NASD=55, NCT=55); age groups, comorbidity and medication-class tables reported.
SPM8 realignment-based estimation of 6 rigid-body motion parameters fully described as the analysis 'pipeline' (since motion itself, not BOLD connectivity, is the outcome).
ASD/CT group membership drawn from the ABIDE phenotypic file; ADOS mentioned as available but the paper does not restate the diagnostic criteria used to assign ASD status.
Age-group stratification (G1-G5), site-level breakdowns, comorbidity and medication class are all explicitly examined as potential confounders/modifiers.
Separate analyses performed by site, age group, medication status (naive vs. 2+ vs. 3+ medications) and comorbidity status rather than pooling uncritically.
Outcome is a validated stochastic (Gamma-distribution noise-to-signal ratio) characterisation of micro-movement waveforms, methodologically detailed.

Non-parametric distributional analyses (K-S tests) and confidence-interval comparisons are used extensively, but explicit correction for the large number of site x age x medication subgroup comparisons is not clearly described.

risk_of_bias.summary: A methodologically unusual but well-specified associational ABIDE study that repurposes raw resting-state fMRI head-motion time series as the outcome of interest, with explicit site-level inclusion criteria and per-site/per-subgroup N, though diagnostic-instrument detail and multiple-comparisons correction are less explicit.

charting.title: Motor noise is rich signal in autism research and pharmacological treatments
charting.comorbidities_included_excluded: 79 ASD participants had comorbidity data (NYU site); 41 of these had one or more comorbid diagnoses
charting.medications_therapies: Medication class recorded and analysed (medication-naive vs. 2+ vs. 3+ medications)
charting.severity_levels: Autism severity examined as a modifier of noise patterns
charting.data_types: resting-state fMRI (head-motion parameter time series, not BOLD connectivity)
charting.feature_types: head micro-movement kinematics (linear and angular speed)
charting.specific_features: Noise-to-signal ratio and Gamma-distribution shape/scale parameters of linear and angular head-motion speed, derived from SPM8 realignment parameters
charting.feature_extraction_tools: SPM8 (realign/estimate-reslice) applied to raw, uncorrected resting-state scans
charting.feature_change_direction: Increased noise-to-signal ratio and randomness of head micro-movements in ASD vs. controls
charting.validation_methodology: Non-parametric (distributional) statistical comparisons (e.g. Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests) across sites, age groups and medication subgroups
charting.summary_key_findings: Analysing raw (uncorrected) resting-state fMRI head-motion time series from 605 ABIDE I participants (304 ASD, 301 controls) across 7 sites, this study finds significantly excess noise and randomness in head micro-movements for ASD participants, worsening with comorbid diagnoses, lower IQ and greater autism severity, and present regardless of psychotropic medication status.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Head micro-movement noise-to-signal ratio (linear and angular speed)
charting.reviewer_notes: This paper treats head motion extracted from resting-state fMRI scans as the biological signal of interest (not a nuisance to regress out), which is an unusual use of ABIDE rs-fMRI data relative to connectivity-based studies in this corpus.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE I; 605 participants (304 ASD, 301 typically developing controls) from 7 of 16 sites (UM_1, UM_2, USM, NYU, UCLA_1, OLIN, PITT) with raw, uncorrected resting-state scans
narrative_row.methods: SPM8 realignment used to extract 6 rigid-body head-motion parameters from raw resting-state scans; Gamma-distribution noise-to-signal ratio and shape/scale parameters computed for linear and angular micro-movement speed; non-parametric distributional comparisons across sites, age groups, comorbidity and medication subgroups
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD participants show significantly excess noise-to-signal ratio and randomness in head micro-movements relative to controls, consistently across sites, worsening with comorbidity, lower IQ, and greater autism severity, and present regardless of medication status
narrative_row.key_limitations: Diagnostic instrument/criteria for ASD/CT labels not restated; explicit multiple-comparisons correction across the many site x age x medication subgroup tests not clearly described; medication dosage and treatment duration data unavailable
narrative_row.relevance_notes: An unconventional ABIDE analysis that repurposes head-motion time series (typically treated as a nuisance to regress out) as the primary biological signal, with explicit, reconstructible per-site inclusion criteria and N
